Contour plots of predicted outcomes

contour.DLNMLPS_pred.Rd

Produce contour plots of predicted outcomes obtained from pred_crossbasis(). In contrast to plot.dlnmLPS_pred(), this function only produces contour plots of surfaces and therefore is only available for plot configurations that result in a three-dimensional surface. For Poisson or negative binomial models with a log link, relative risks (RRs) are plotted; for binomial models with a logit link, odds ratios (ORs) are plotted; and for Gaussian models with an identity link, additive differences in the outcome are plotted.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'dlnmLPS_pred'
contour(
  x,
  slice_lag = NULL,
  slice_x = NULL,
  slice_y = NULL,
  slice_by = NULL,
  ptype = "overall",
  xlim = NULL,
  ylim = NULL,
  zlim = NULL,
  cols = NULL,
  xlab = NULL,
  ylab = NULL,
  zlab = NULL,
  mar = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An object returned by pred_crossbasis().

slice_lag

Lag value(s) at which to obtain slices. Integer or numeric vector.

slice_x

Exposure values of the first exposure variable at which to obtain slices. Integer or numeric vector.

slice_y

Exposure values of the second exposure variable at which to obtain slices (bivariate exposures only). Integer or numeric vector.

slice_by

Optional argument to specify the levels of the by-variable to be plotted. One value or multiple values supplied through a vector.

ptype

Character string specifying the type of plot. One of:

"overall"

Overall cumulative exposure-response plot.

"cross"

Complete exposure-lag-response surface (only available for univariate exposures).

"slices"

Slices through the exposure-lag-response surface.

xlim, ylim, zlim

Numeric vectors of length two giving axis limits.

cols

Colours used for lines, surfaces or contours.

xlab, ylab, zlab

Axis labels.

mar

Figure margins.

...

Additional graphical arguments passed to the underlying plotting functions. For 3D plots, additional arguments of graphics::perspcan be passed.

Value

Produces a contour plot and returns NULL invisibly.

Details

This function provides contour representations of the three-dimensional surfaces available in plot.dlnmLPS_pred().

The available plots are:

  • the exposure-lag-response surface (ptype = "cross") for univariate exposures;

  • the overall cumulative exposure-response surface (ptype = "overall") for bivariate exposures when no exposure slice is specified;

  • slice surfaces (ptype = "slices") whenever the selected slicing variables define a three-dimensional surface.

Contour plots are not available for two-dimensional plots (e.g., cumulative exposure-response curves or exposure/lag slices shown as multiple lines). Confidence intervals are therefore not supported.

See also

plot.dlnmLPS_pred(), pred_crossbasis()

Examples

data(barcelona_temp)
data(shapefile_bcn)

# Examples of applications

dataset <- barcelona_temp |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dow = weekdays(date),
    year = lubridate::year(date),
    month = lubridate::month(date)
  )

group <- factor(paste0(dataset$District, "-", dataset$year))


### Example 1: Unpenalized and spatially varying DLNM

# Create the (unpenalized) crossbasis
knots_max <- quantile(dataset$Tmax, probs = c(0.10,0.50,0.90))
knots_lag <- dlnm::logknots(0:14, nk = 2)

basis.max_unpen <- dlnm::crossbasis(
    dataset$Tmax,
    argvar=list(fun = "ns", knots = knots_max),
    arglag=list(fun="ns", knots = knots_lag),
    lag=14,
    group=group
)

# Fit model
model_max_spat <- dlnmLPS(
    dtot ~ 1 + factor(dow) +
    sm(month, arg = list(type = "ns", df = 3)) +
    sm(year, arg = list(type = "rw1")) +
    sm(basis.max_unpen, by = District,
            arg.by = list(type = "Leroux", map = shapefile_bcn)) +
    sm(District, arg = list(type = "Leroux", map = shapefile_bcn)),
    data = dataset,
    offset = log(pop),
    model.comparison = list(DIC = TRUE),
    family = "Poisson")

summary(model_max_spat)

# Make predictions
pred_spat_max <- pred_crossbasis(
    basis.max_unpen,
    model_max_spat,
    at_x = 22:30,
    cen = 25,
    lag = c(0,14),
    CI = TRUE,
    by = unique(dataset$District)
)

# Plot results (region-specific overal RR)
plot(pred_spat_max, ptype = "overall", CI = TRUE, xlab = "temp", ylab = "RR", ylim = c(0.9,3.0))





### Example 2: Unpenalized and deprivation-varying DLNM

# Fit model
model_max_conf <- dlnmLPS(
    dtot ~ 1 + factor(dow) +
    sm(month, arg = list(type = "ns", df = 3)) +
    sm(year, arg = list(type = "rw1")) +
    sm(depriv, arg = list(type = "ns", df = 3)) +
    sm(basis.max_unpen, by = depriv,
            arg.by = list(type = "ns", df = 3)) +
    sm(District, arg = list(type = "Leroux", map = shapefile_bcn)),
    data = dataset,
    offset = log(pop),
    model.comparison = list(DIC = TRUE),
    family = "Poisson")

# Make predictions
pred_conf_max <- pred_crossbasis(
    basis.max_unpen,
    model_max_conf,
    at_x = 22:30,
    cen = 25,
    lag = c(0,14),
    CI = TRUE,
    by = quantile(dataset$depriv,probs= c(0.10, 0.90))
)

# Plot results (contour plot exposure-lag-response)
contour(pred_conf_max, ptype = "cross", cols = function(n) hcl.colors(n, "Inferno"))




### Example 3: Penalized and common DLNM

# Create the (penalized) crossbasis
basis.max <- dlnm::crossbasis(
    dataset$Tmax,
    argvar = list(df = 5, fun = "ps"),
    arglag = list(df = 5, fun = "ps"),
    lag = 14,
    group = group
)

# Fit model
model_max_common <- dlnmLPS(
    dtot ~ 1 + factor(dow) +
    sm(month, arg = list(type = "ns", df = 3)) +
    sm(year, arg = list(type = "rw1")) +
    sm(basis.max, arg = list(pen= 2)) +
    sm(District, arg = list(type = "Leroux", map = shapefile_bcn)),
    data = dataset,
    offset = log(pop),
    model.comparison = list(DIC = TRUE),
    family = "Poisson"
)

# Make predictions
pred_max <- pred_crossbasis(
     basis = basis.max,
     model = model_max_common,
     at_x = 22:30,
     cen = 25,
     lag = c(0,14),
     CI = TRUE
)

# Plot results (lag-specific and overall RR)
plot(pred_max, slice_lag = c(0,3,8), ptype = "slices", CI = TRUE, xlab = "temp", ylab = "RR")

plot(pred_max, ptype = "overall", CI = TRUE, xlab = "temp", ylab = "RR")



### Example 4: Penalized and common joint DLNM

# Create the (penalized) joint crossbasis
basis.max_min <- joint.crossbasis(
    cbind(dataset$Tmax, dataset$Tmin),
    argvar1 = list(df = 5, fun = "ps"),
    argvar2 = list(df = 5, fun = "ps"),
    arglag = list(df = 5, fun = "ps"),
    lag = 14,
    group = group
)

# Fit model
model_joint_common <- dlnmLPS(
    dtot ~ 1 + factor(dow) +
    sm(month, arg = list(type = "ns", df = 3)) +
    sm(year, arg = list(type = "rw1")) +
    sm(basis.max_min, arg = list(pen= 2)) +
    sm(District, arg = list(type = "Leroux", map = shapefile_bcn)),
    data = dataset,
    offset = log(pop),
    model.comparison = list(DIC = TRUE),
    family = "Poisson"
)

# Make predictions
pred_max_min <- pred_crossbasis(
     basis = basis.max_min,
     model = model_joint_common,
     at_x = c(29,29,29,30,30,30,31,31,31),
     at_y = c(20,21,22,20,21,22,20,21,22),
     cen = c(25,15),
     lag = c(0,14),
     CI = TRUE
)

# Plot results (contour plot overall RR)
contour(pred_max_min, ptype = "overall", cols = function(n) hcl.colors(n, "Inferno"))
